title: IndustriAll Europe union protest at European Parliament in Strasbourg

tea.why: Metal and textile workers are protesting against job insecurity, layoffs, and the shift of investments towards the defense sector.
tea.want: Workers are demanding favorable conditions within the upcoming Industrial Accelerator Act to protect and revive European industry.
tea.changed: Nov 24: IndustriAll Europe organized a demonstration of workers outside the European Parliament in Strasbourg.

summary: On November 24, 2026, a large delegation of metal and textile workers gathered outside the European Parliament in Strasbourg for a mobilization organized by IndustriAll Europe. Protesters from various industrial sectors converged to voice concerns regarding widespread layoffs, increasing reliance on temporary unemployment schemes, and fears that corporate focus on defense investments could jeopardize civilian manufacturing jobs. According to the sources, participants highlighted vulnerabilities in the European labor market, including competition from foreign imports and rising energy pressures. The demonstration coincided with discussions surrounding the upcoming Industrial Accelerator Act, with participants seeking strong regulatory protections and favorable conditions to safeguard European manufacturing employment.
demands: Favorable conditions in the Industrial Accelerator Act
Protection and revival of European industry
Safeguarding jobs in the metal and chemical sectors
response: No official response reported in the sources.

updates.text: IndustriAll Europe union members and workers demonstrated outside the European Parliament in Strasbourg.
